Markdown

Markdown is a lightweight markup language for creating formatted text using a plain-text editor. It is widely used in documentation, readme files, forums and note-taking tools across the web.

Markdown
Filename extensions.md, .markdown[1]
Type of format
  • Markup language
  • Plain text
Syntax noteUse a | b for alternatives
Example
# Heading
*emphasis*

The language was created in 2004 by John Gruber with Aaron Swartz, with the goal of letting people write in an easy-to-read plain text format that converts to structurally valid HTML.

Layout cell oneLayout cell two
 Side text in a layout table.

Many variants extend the original syntax with tables, footnotes and task lists, and the CommonMark project specifies a standard core that implementations can share.
